g.text: The supplied breach index reports this address in 80 collections, but every
entry lacks a date and exposed-field list. The high rating comes from breadth of
exposure, not confirmed credentials. No accounts or hostnames were returned.
Only one source was queried: breach_index (backed by xposedornot). It returned
unavailable_sources is empty, so no source is known to have failed or been
Treat the address as widely circulated: assume it is on credential-stuffing
lists and stop using it as a login identifier for any account that matters.
Change the password on every account registered to test@example.com, starting
with the platforms named above (LinkedIn, Twitter, Patreon, Chegg, SoundCloud,
Last.fm, Roblox), and set a unique password per site via a password manager.
Enable phishing-resistant MFA (passkey or hardware key, then TOTP app) on
those accounts; do not rely on SMS where another factor is offered.
